key_insight: MXNorm reuses block-scale metadata produced by MXFP-style low-precision matrix-multiply units to approximate RMSNorm statistics, enabling tensor normalisation without expensive high-precision reductions or extra elementwise passes.
problem_solved: Reduces the performance and precision mismatch between highly-optimized low-precision matrix multiplication and slower, higher-precision reductions/elementwise ops used for normalization, which limit throughput on modern accelerators.
method: Intercept and reuse MXFP block scale factors emitted during low-precision matmul to approximate per-block second-moment / RMS statistics.
Compute normalization using those reused scales (and minimal extra correction) in lower precision, avoiding full-precision global reductions and elementwise passes.
Provide a drop-in replacement for RMSNorm that preserves compatibility with existing models while shifting the reduction workload onto already-available MXFP metadata.
impact: Enables faster and more hardware-efficient model training/inference on accelerators that use low-precision formats by removing a key software bottleneck (reductions/elementwise ops), improving throughput and energy efficiency with minimal model changes.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: standard matmul + separate high-precision normalization vs. MXNorm reusing MXFP block scales (showing removed reduction path).

paper_title: MXNorm: Reusing MXFP block scales for efficient tensor normalisation
paper_authors: Callum McLean, Luke Y. Prince, Alexandre Payot, Paul Balança, Carlo Luschi
